description: OpenAPI Backend parity (Algorithm A-OAS, feature F-12). The runner builds a Registry from each `document` via the backend entry point (load_spec -> OpenAPIScanner.scan -> projection -> HTTPProxyRegistryWriter.write) and asserts the registered module set, the repaired descriptions, the emitted diagnostics, and the resulting Agent Card. The scanner's own derivation is NOT restated here -- it is pinned by apcore-toolkit's own 24-case corpus. What this fixture owns is everything the binding adds on top: the apcore-registry ID projection (FR-OAS-002), the empty-description repair (FR-OAS-003), the path-typed spec key (FR-OAS-004), the unapproved-write warning (FR-OAS-005), and the collision preflight (FR-OAS-006). Every expectation was MEASURED against apcore-toolkit 0.11.1 / apcore 0.30.0 by running the real scanner, never derived from reading the algorithm.
notes: Every case spells out its full `document` rather than referencing a shared base, so a driver never has to merge fragments.
`expected_modules[].description` is the description AFTER the FR-OAS-003 repair. A case whose operation carries a summary asserts the repair did NOT fire.

Annotations are asserted against apcore's own ModuleAnnotations field names (readonly/destructive/idempotent/open_world/requires_approval), never against a transport-specific projection. apcore-mcp's fixture asserts MCP ToolAnnotations hint names; that column has no A2A counterpart and is deliberately absent.
`requires_approval` is asserted false on every write-method case. It is pinned as a FACT so the gap cannot be closed accidentally in one language: the scanner never infers it, for any method.

The path-derived id for `/users/{userId}` measures as `users.userid.get` on apcore-toolkit 0.11.1 -- the brace parameter contributes its name lowercased, with no underscore inserted. Do not 'correct' this to `users.user_id.get`.
Not pinned here: the scanner's module_id derivation, `metadata.openapi.*` contents, proxy request shaping, and upstream HTTP error wording. All belong to apcore-toolkit or to the deployment.

DRIVER REQUIREMENT: a runner MUST fail loudly when a case group named here is absent or empty, and MUST NOT fall back to an empty list. Measured 2026-09-07 by renaming `test_cases`: apcore-a2a-python failed at collection (it indexes the key), while the TypeScript runner silently dropped from 46 passing tests to 33 and the Rust runner reported 9 passing while asserting nothing. Both used an `?? []` / `unwrap_or_default()` fallback. A group rename in this file must never be able to turn a runner green. Skipping the whole suite when the spec repo is absent is a separate, legitimate case.

test_cases.description: FR-OAS-002. The toolkit sanitizes to [A-Za-z0-9_.-]; apcore's registry accepts only ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)*$. Without the projection this module does not register and the Agent Card is empty.
FR-OAS-002 rule 2. A hyphen is legal to the toolkit and illegal to apcore; the dots are segment separators and survive.

DISCRIMINATING CASE for FR-OAS-002. An apcore segment may not begin with a digit, so `2fa` cannot be repaired without inventing an ID. The module is dropped -- and because the projection runs inside the scanner's transform_module hook, a hook returning None drops it SILENTLY. An implementation that merely drops the module passes every other assertion in this group and fails this one. The sibling operation must still register: one bad operation does not fail the scan.

FR-OAS-002 ordering. `listPets` and `listpets` are two distinct operations to OpenAPI and one module ID to apcore -- the projection CREATES a collision the document did not have. Projecting after the scanner's deduplicate_ids would register one and lose the other with no warning. Measured: the scanner renames the second and attaches the warning itself.
FR-OAS-002 with `prefix`. The prefix is the scanner's base_path_prefix and is already part of the derived ID when the projection sees it.

DISCRIMINATING CASE for FR-OAS-003, and A2A-specific. The operation carries neither summary nor description, so the scanner yields `""` -- and AgentCardBuilder skips any module whose description is empty. Composed naively those two correct behaviours drop the operation from the Agent Card with no diagnostic. The repair synthesizes `{METHOD} {url_path}` from the metadata keys the writer already requires.
FR-OAS-003. A whitespace-only summary reaches the module verbatim and is exactly as unusable as an absent one -- AgentCardBuilder trims before testing, so it skips this too.
FR-OAS-003 negative case. The repair must not fire when the scanner produced a usable description. Measured: with no summary, the scanner takes the FIRST LINE of `description`.

get.description:
First line here.
Second line ignored.

test_cases.description: The positive counterpart to `no_base_url_anywhere_rejected`, and the only case that can detect an implementation silently ignoring `base_url`. The document has NO `servers`, so the option is the sole source; an implementation that drops the key fails here with the same 'no base_url' error the negative case asserts. Every other case in this corpus supplies `servers[0].url`, which masks the defect.

The full method-to-annotation table, measured. GET is readonly+cacheable; PUT is idempotent; DELETE is destructive; POST and PATCH carry NO behavioural annotation at all. open_world is true throughout -- these modules do call an external system. requires_approval is false for EVERY method including DELETE: the scanner never infers it, which is the gap FR-OAS-005 warns about.

warning_cases.description: FR-OAS-005. Any of POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE with requires_approval false and no acknowledgement produces the warning. The message must name the public Agent Card, because that is the A2A-specific exposure: the route is auth-exempt and A2A clients are built to crawl it.
FR-OAS-005 suppression 1: nothing to warn about. A document of GETs only.
FR-OAS-005 suppression 3: an explicit recorded operator decision. The ONLY configuration flag that suppresses it.

DISCRIMINATING CASE for FR-OAS-005. An ACL is attached and it permits everything -- so nothing will ever ask for approval, and the warning must still fire. apcore's own GovernanceState.unprotected_control_surface states the rule this follows: it reports the ABSENCE OF A GATE, never the presence of protection; a wired ACL that permits every call still yields false. An implementation that gates the warning on governance_state().acl_configured passes every other case in this group and fails this one.

config_cases.description: FR-OAS-004 rule 1. A value beginning http:// or https:// is a URL: never path-resolved, never made absolute, despite a project_root and a differing cwd both being set. The discriminator is the scheme prefix, not a guess from the string's shape.

FR-OAS-004 rule 3. Against Config.project_root, NOT the process CWD. The differing cwd is what makes this case assert anything -- apcore-mcp's TypeScript and Rust config routes silently resolve against CWD here, which this fixture exists to prevent in this binding.

FR-OAS-004 rule 2. A set-but-empty value (from APCORE_A2A_OPENAPI_SPEC= or spec: "") is discarded with a WARNING and resolution falls through to the next tier. It must NOT be joined to a base, which would silently yield the project root -- exactly the failure apcore closed for APCORE_ACL_ROOT= and whose fix does not reach a consumer namespace.
FR-OAS-004 rule 3, absolute branch. An absolute path is already resolved and project_root must not be prepended.

card_cases.description: The exposure FR-OAS-005 warns about, pinned as a fact rather than left implicit. A scanned write operation is neither ACL-denied to @external nor approval-gated, so the 0.6.0 public-card filter subtracts nothing and it appears on the anonymous, auth-exempt discovery document. This case exists so that a future change to card visibility cannot silently alter the exposure without failing a test.

The recommended remedy, and the reason the backend does NOT withhold scanned write operations as a class. An ACL rule carrying approval: required both gates the call and removes the skill from the public card (FR-AGC-003 criterion 11), while the extended card -- served to an authenticated caller -- still advertises it. One configuration change closes the discovery exposure and the invocation gap together.

error_cases.description: OpenAPIScanner.scan refuses anything that is not 3.0.x / 3.1.x. Only the fragment '3.0' is pinned, never the toolkit's full sentence -- the wording belongs to apcore-toolkit and may change without breaking this contract.
No base_url option and no usable absolute servers[0].url. A relative or templated server URL counts as absent.

FR-OAS-006. When an extensions directory is also configured, `prefix` is mandatory: the scanner deduplicates within one scan only and knows nothing about modules already in the registry. Checked FIRST, before any fetch or scan, so a misconfiguration fails without a network round trip.

FR-OAS-006. TWO collisions are seeded deliberately: both must be named, because an implementation reporting only the first forces one restart per collision. The registry must be byte-for-byte unchanged afterwards -- toolkit writers report per-module WriteResults and never abort, so without a preflight a duplicate arrives as a failed WriteResult, gets logged and skipped, and leaves a partial registry: a skill the document advertises, absent from the card, with one log line as the only notice.
